protocol.description: Causal LM teacher forcing on each text independently. Single forward pass; each text fits in context. Encoding uses add_special_tokens=False (none of these three tokenizers prepends BOS). The first token is shown but not scored. Log-probabilities come from a float32 softmax of the logits. n_bytes_text is the UTF-8 length of the raw text; n_bytes_scored is the UTF-8 length of the concatenated scored tokens. cross_entropy_nats is the mean negative log-likelihood over scored tokens; perplexity is exp of that mean (token-level); bits_per_byte is total NLL in nats / (ln(2) * n_bytes_scored). Per-token multiclass Brier is ||p - onehot||^2 = ||p||^2 + 1 - 2 p_y, computed from the full float32 softmax (not from the top-k list). mean_brier is the average of those token Brier scores.

texts.title: A short philosophy-of-science sentence
texts.text: A strictly proper scoring rule is uniquely optimized by reporting one's true probabilities, which is why log loss remains the natural training objective for a probabilistic language model.

texts.title: A tiny Python function
texts.text:
def bits_per_byte(total_nll_nats, n_bytes):
    return total_nll_nats / (math.log(2) * n_bytes)
